## 🔵 SPUTNIK 1 — The World's First Satellite (1957)

Sputnik 1 was the first artificial Earth satellite, launched into an elliptical low Earth orbit by the Soviet Union on **4 October 1957**.

### Design & Size
Weighing approximately **83.6 kilograms (184 pounds)**, Sputnik 1 was a polished aluminum sphere with a diameter of **58 centimeters (23 inches)**, equipped with four long antennas.

### Technology & Instruments
The satellite consisted of a pressurized, highly polished aluminium shell, which contained **two 1-watt transmitters**, three silver-zinc batteries and one ventilator. The transmitters were connected to four whip antennas — two 2.4 m long and two 2.9 m long.

There were **no scientific instruments** on board, but the transmitters changed their transmission pattern if the temperature of the satellite's interior went outside the nominal range or if internal pressure dropped.

### Orbit & Speed
It traveled at an average speed of **29,000 km/h (18,000 mph)** and completed an orbit around the Earth every 96 minutes.

It achieved an orbit with an **apogee of 940 km** and a **perigee of 230 km**.

### Lifespan & Mission
It sent a radio signal back to Earth for **three weeks** before its three silver-zinc batteries became depleted. Aerodynamic drag caused it to fall back into the atmosphere on **4 January 1958**.

The satellite completed about **1,400 orbits** of the Earth over a cumulative distance of **70 million kilometers**.

### Purpose
The craft's primary function was simply **to place a radio transmitter into orbit** around the Earth.

### Historical Impact
The satellite's success was unanticipated by the United States. It precipitated the **American Sputnik crisis** and triggered the start of the **Space Race**.

---

## 🔴 SpainSat NG-II — One of the Most Advanced Satellites (2025)

SpainSat NG-II is considered **one of the most advanced satellites in the world**, and successfully lifted off from Cape Canaveral, Florida, aboard a Falcon 9 rocket.

### Design & Size
SpainSat NG-II measures **7 meters (23 feet)** in length and weighs around **6 tons (12,000 pounds)** — roughly **72 times heavier** than Sputnik 1.

### Technology & Instruments
Based on an **Airbus Eurostar Neo platform**, the spacecraft carries an innovative payload including an **X-band active receive and transmit antenna system**, providing the equivalent functionality of **16 traditional antennas**, and can adapt and change its coverage **up to 1,000 times per second**.

Its advanced flexible-payload technology makes the **tri-band (X, Ka, and UHF)** capability especially valuable for critical communications over extensive areas.

This advanced technology allows the satellite to **detect signal jamming attempts, pinpoint their sources**, and withstand electromagnetic pulses related to nuclear events.

### Orbit
SpainSat NG operates from **geostationary orbit (GEO)**, approximately **36,000 km** above the Earth — far higher than Sputnik's low Earth orbit.

### Lifespan & Mission
The SpainSat NG satellites are designed for an **operational useful life of 15 years**, remaining in service until 2040.

### Purpose
The programme is designed to provide **military-grade secure communications** to the Spanish Armed Forces and international organisations such as the European Commission under GOVSATCOM, NATO, and other allied governments.

Together with its twin, it forms a constellation covering **nearly two-thirds of the planet**, from the Americas to Asia, including Europe, Africa and the Middle East.

### Investment
With an investment of **over 2 billion euros**, the new satellites incorporate cutting-edge dual military and civilian technology, including the most advanced active antennas in Europe.
